title: Request Body Is Always 33 Bytes Larger Than Expected Size
body:
### First Check

- [X] I added a very descriptive title here.
- [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search.
- [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information.
- [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer.
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
@app.post("/transcribe_android_test")
async def receive_data(request: Request):
    content_type = audio_request.headers.get("content-type")
    if content_type != "application/octet-stream":
        print("Unsupported Media Type")
    bytes_data: bytes = await request.body()
    size = sys.getsizeof(bytes_data)
    print(f"Size of bytes: {size} bytes")
```


### Description

I have an Android client app, which sends a byte array of audio data to the server:

` val requestBody: RequestBody = RequestBody.create(contentType = "application/octet-stream".toMediaTypeOrNull(), content = dataByteArray)`
            
`Log.d("Main", "request body size: ${requestBody.contentLength()}")
`

As you can see from this screenshot of the Logcat message:

![Screenshot_2025-04-08_13-12-54](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b3b2f0e1-1031-47ea-a98a-a2b7086f8e8a)

The size of the byte array sent is **31744**.

From Ngrok's traffic inspector, I'm able to confirm that the data of the exact same size is able to be received:

![Screenshot_2025-04-08_13-15-59](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f65c1aa-6117-4c5d-b8b1-08c5693b7a16)

However, there seems to be 33 extra bytes received on FastApi's end:

`bytes_data: bytes = await request.body()`
`size = sys.getsizeof(bytes_data)`
`print(f"Size of bytes: {size} bytes")`

As you can see from the following screenshot:

![Screenshot_2025-04-08_13-21-14](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f0014e0-45ee-4ab3-b0e4-e4f219ce1501)

`request.body()` returns **31777** bytes of data, which is 33 bytes larger than expected. Why is this the case? And how can it be resolved? Thanks in advance!








### Operating System

Linux

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.115.12

### Pydantic Version

2.11.2

### Python Version

3.11.11

### Additional Context

_No response_

answer.body:
@rabyunghwa,

Have a look at the souce code reference of the Request class: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/reference/request/
Methods: `async def stream()`, `async def body()`
It seems that Starlette processes request data as a bytestring.
Probably this is the reason of those extra 33 bytes. :smiley:

You can double-check this hypothesis by writing a unit test !  

And it turns out that `sys.getsizeof()` is not showing what we normally expect it to:
https://nedbatchelder.com/blog/202002/sysgetsizeof_is_not_what_you_want.html

``` python

import os
import sys

data = [os.urandom(0), os.urandom(1), os.urandom(2)]

print([(item, sys.getsizeof(item)) for item in data])
```

All in all there is a room for investigation :smile:

... and I forgot to mention, that you are not showing us the response tab ... :smile:

[Corrections added]
